full_text:
यूपी में बढ़ने लगा कोहरा और धुंध; अब होगी जाड़े की शुरुआत, रात के तापमान में गिरावट
प्रदूषण के कारण 2 दिनों तक धुंध और कोहरे में वृद्धि हो सकती है.
लखनऊ: यूपी में हल्की ठंडक की शुरुआत हो गई है. सुबह और शाम के समय पड़ने वाले धुंध के साथ कोहरे में भी हल्की वृद्धि हुई है. रात के तापमान में कुछ इलाकों में 2 से 4 डिग्री सेल्सियस की कमी दर्ज की गई. वहीं ज्यादातर इलाकों में रात और दिन का तापमान सामान्य व सामान्य के आसपास चल रहा है. सुबह और शाम के समय हल्की गुलाबी सर्दी पड़ रही है. दिन के समय धूप खिलने से मौसम सामान्य बना हुआ है.
मौसम विज्ञान विभाग के अनुसार आने वाले 7 दिनों में मौसम ऐसा ही बना रहेगा. अधिकतम और न्यूनतम तापमान में कोई विशेष बदलाव होने की संभावना नहीं है. प्रदूषण के कारण 2 दिनों तक धुंध और कोहरे में वृद्धि हो सकती है.
लखनऊ का मौसम ऐसा रहेगा: मौसम विज्ञान विभाग के अनुसार सोमवार को लखनऊ में सुबह-शाम के समय हल्की धुंध छाई रहेगी. अधिकतम तापमान में 2 डिग्री सेल्सियस की गिरावट हो सकती है, अधिकतम तापमान 29 और न्यूनतम तापमान 17 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने की संभावना है.
झांसी सबसे गर्म जिला: रविवार को भी उत्तर प्रदेश का झांसी सबसे अधिक गर्म जिला रहा, जहां पर अधिकतम तापमान 33.4 डिग्री सेल्सियस रिकॉर्ड किया गया जो कि सामान्य से 2 डिग्री सेल्सियस अधिक है. वहीं सबसे कम न्यूनतम तापमान 14.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस लखीमपुर खीरी में रिकॉर्ड किया गया जो कि सामान्य से 1 डिग्री सेल्सियस अधिक है.
मौसम वैज्ञानिक डॉक्टर अतुल सिंह ने बताया कि आने वाले 7 दिनों तक उत्तर प्रदेश में मौसम ड्राई बना रहेगा, बारिश की संभावना नहीं है. अधिकतम और न्यूनतम तापमान में भी कोई खास बदलाव नहीं होगा. सुबह-शाम के समय पड़ने वाले धुंध में 1-2 दिन तक इजाफा हो सकता है.

छठ पूजा के दौरान झारखंड में बारिश की संभावना।
9 से 15 नवंबर तक झारखंड के मौसम में दिखेगा उतार-चढ़ाव।
रांची समेत छह जिलों में गरज-चमक के साथ हो सकती है बारिश।
डिजिटल डेस्क, रांची। झारखंड में नवंबर की शुरुआत के साथ ही मौसम का मिजाज बदलने लगा है। सुबह और शाम के समय हल्की ठंड महसूस होने लगी है, जबकि दोपहर में धूप निकलने से गर्मी का असर बना हुआ है। राज्य के कई हिस्सों में सुबह हल्की धुंध और कुहासा भी देखने को मिल रहा है।
इस बीच मौसम विभाग ने आज 9 से 15 नवंबर तक के मौसम का पूर्वानुमान जारी किया है। इसके अनुसार, झारखंड के ज्यादातर जिलों में मौसम शुष्क रहने की संभावना है। हालांकि, संताल परगना के कुछ इलाकों में हल्की बारिश और गरज-चमक हो सकती है।
झारखंड के इन छह जिलों में हो सकती है हल्की बारिश
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, आज 9 नवंबर को राजधानी रांची में सुबह हल्का कुहासा छाया रह सकता है। वहीं, दिन में आसमान आंशिक रूप से बादलों से ढका रहने का अनुमान है। इस दौरान रांची का अधिकतम तापमान 27 डिग्री और न्यूनतम तापमान 16 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रह सकता है।
वहीं, देवघर, दुमका, जामताड़ा, गोड्डा, पाकुड़ और साहिबगंज में कुछ स्थानों पर हल्की बारिश होने की संभावना है। इन जिलों में गरज-चमक भी हो सकती है। इसके अलावा राज्य के बाकी 18 जिलों में बारिश के आसार नहीं हैं। यहां मौसम शुष्क बना रह सकता है।
रांची से पलामू तक तापमान में उतार-चढ़ाव
झारखंड में इन दिनों अधिकतम और न्यूनतम तापमान में उतार-चढ़ाव देखने को मिल रहा है। दिन में धूप के कारण गर्मी का एहसास होता है, जबकि सुबह और देर रात हल्की ठंड महसूस होने लगी है।
प्रमुख जिलों के तापमान की बात करें तो रांची में अधिकतम तापमान 28 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 19 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया है। वहीं, पलामू, बोकारो, हजारीबाग और रामगढ़ में अधिकतम तापमान 29 डिग्री सेल्सियस है। इन जिलों में न्यूनतम तापमान क्रमशः 17, 20, 19 और 18 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा।
इन पांच जिलों में ठंड का असर ज्यादा
राज्य के पठारी और ऊंचाई वाले इलाकों में ठंड का असर दूसरे क्षेत्रों की तुलना में अधिक महसूस किया जा रहा है। सुबह और शाम के समय तापमान कम रहने से लोगों को ठंड का एहसास होने लगा है। गुमला, लोहरदगा, पलामू, हजारीबाग और रांची में ठंड का असर बढ़ रहा है। खासकर गुमला में तापमान में लगातार गिरावट देखने को मिल रही है।
9 से 14 नवंबर तक कैसा रहेगा झारखंड का मौसम?
मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक, नवंबर के दूसरे सप्ताह में झारखंड के मौसम में उतार-चढ़ाव जारी रहेगा।
9 नवंबर को सुबह हल्की धुंध छाई रह सकती है, जबकि दिन में आंशिक बादल रहेंगे। उत्तर-पूर्वी जिलों में हल्की बारिश की संभावना है। 10 नवंबर को कुछ इलाकों में बादल छाए रहने के साथ गरज-चमक और हल्की बारिश हो सकती है।
11 नवंबर को रांची में सुबह कुहासा और दिन में आंशिक बादल देखने को मिल सकते हैं। इसके बाद 12 नवंबर को आसमान मुख्य रूप से साफ रहने और धूप निकलने का अनुमान है। 13 नवंबर को सुबह हल्की धुंध के बाद मौसम साफ हो सकता है। वहीं, 14 नवंबर को राज्य के ज्यादातर हिस्सों में आसमान साफ रहने के साथ मौसम शुष्क बना रह सकता है।
छठ पूजा पर कैसा रहेगा मौसम?
छठ पूजा के दौरान मौसम की स्थिति श्रद्धालुओं के लिए काफी महत्वपूर्ण है। खासकर सुबह और शाम के अर्घ्य के समय मौसम कैसा रहेगा, इस पर लोगों की नजर है।
मौसम के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक, नवंबर के मध्य तक सुबह हल्की धुंध और ठंडी हवाएं महसूस हो सकती हैं। हालांकि, 15 नवंबर के लिए भारतीय मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (IMD) की ओर से कोई अलर्ट जारी नहीं किया गया है। ऐसे में सुबह अर्घ्य देने के लिए घाटों पर जाने वाले छठ व्रतियों को गर्म कपड़े साथ रखने की सलाह दी गई है।
झारखंड में आने वाले दिनों में और बढ़ेगी ठंड?
झारखंड में धीरे-धीरे सर्दी का असर बढ़ने लगा है। रांची, गुमला, लोहरदगा, पलामू और हजारीबाग जैसे जिलों में सुबह और रात के समय ठंड महसूस की जा रही है। हालांकि, दिन में धूप निकलने से तापमान बढ़ जाता है और लोगों को राहत मिलती है।
फिलहाल मौसम में उतार-चढ़ाव जारी रहने की संभावना है। वहीं, रात के तापमान में गिरावट के साथ आने वाले दिनों में झारखंड के कई जिलों में ठंड का असर और बढ़ सकता है।

title: एक शीत मोर्चा आगे बढ़ रहा है, जिसके चलते कुछ क्षेत्रों में तापमान 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे गिर गया है। - Vietnam.vn

full_text:
एक शीत मोर्चा आगे बढ़ रहा है, जिसके चलते कुछ क्षेत्रों में तापमान 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे गिर गया है।
जीडी एंड टीडी - एक शक्तिशाली शीत मोर्चा आ गया है, जिससे उत्तर में ठंड का मौसम है, कुछ क्षेत्रों में तापमान 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे गिर गया है; मध्य क्षेत्र में व्यापक भारी बारिश का दौर शुरू हो रहा है।
कल रात और आज सुबह (9 नवंबर) को, एक शीत मोर्चे ने उत्तरी वियतनाम के पहाड़ी और मध्यभूमि क्षेत्रों को प्रभावित किया।
उत्तरी वियतनाम और उत्तर मध्य वियतनाम में हल्की बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, उत्तरी डेल्टा के दक्षिणी भाग, थान्ह होआ और न्घे आन प्रांत के उत्तरी भाग में मध्यम से भारी बारिश होगी; रात 1 बजे तापमान आमतौर पर 22-25 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा, और पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में 18-21 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा; को तो विशेष क्षेत्र में, 6 स्तर की तेज़ उत्तर-पूर्वी हवाएँ चलेंगी, जिनकी तीव्रता 8 स्तर तक पहुँच सकती है।
9 नवंबर से, ठंडी हवा का प्रभाव पूर्वोत्तर क्षेत्र के अन्य क्षेत्रों में भी पड़ेगा, फिर उत्तर-पश्चिम क्षेत्र, उत्तरी और मध्य मध्य क्षेत्रों और दक्षिण मध्य क्षेत्र के कुछ हिस्सों में भी इसका असर दिखेगा। अंतर्देशीय क्षेत्रों में हवाएं 3-4 स्तर पर उत्तर-पूर्व की ओर मुड़ेंगी; तटीय क्षेत्रों में 5 स्तर की हवाएं चलेंगी, कुछ स्थानों पर ये 6 स्तर तक पहुंच सकती हैं और इनकी तीव्रता 7 स्तर तक जा सकती है।
उत्तरी वियतनाम और उत्तर मध्य वियतनाम में मौसम ठंडा हो रहा है। इस शीतकाल के दौरान उत्तरी वियतनाम और उत्तर मध्य वियतनाम में न्यूनतम तापमान आमतौर पर 15-18 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहता है, जबकि कुछ पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में तापमान 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे भी पहुंच जाता है।
हनोई क्षेत्र में, 9 नवंबर की सुबह तड़के, एक शीत मोर्चे के कारण मध्यम से भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें आईं, कुछ स्थानीय क्षेत्रों में बहुत भारी बारिश हुई; मौसम ठंडा हो गया।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
समुद्र में, 9 नवंबर की दिन और रात के दौरान, टोंकिन की खाड़ी और उत्तरी दक्षिण चीन सागर (होआंग सा विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्र सहित) में, 7 की तीव्रता वाली, कभी-कभी 8 की तीव्रता वाली, और 9-10 की तीव्रता तक के झोंकों वाली तेज़ उत्तरपूर्वी हवाएँ चलेंगी; समुद्री लहरें 4-6 मीटर ऊँची होंगी; टोंकिन की खाड़ी में, 2-4 मीटर ऊँची लहरें होंगी और समुद्र अशांत रहेगा।
मध्य पूर्वी सागर के उत्तरी भाग और दक्षिणी क्वांग त्रि से क्वांग न्गाई तक के समुद्री क्षेत्र में, उत्तरपूर्वी हवा धीरे-धीरे स्तर 6 तक, कभी-कभी स्तर 7 तक, और स्तर 8-9 के झोंकों के साथ मजबूत होगी; समुद्री लहरें 3-5 मीटर ऊंची होंगी; समुद्र अशांत रहेगा।
9 नवंबर की सुबह, उत्तरी डेल्टा क्षेत्र, दक्षिणी फु थो प्रांत, थान्ह होआ और उत्तरी न्घे आन में मध्यम से भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ीं, कुछ क्षेत्रों में बहुत भारी बारिश हुई। दक्षिणी न्घे आन प्रांत में भी 9 नवंबर को भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ीं।
9 नवंबर से 11 नवंबर की रात तक, हा तिन्ह से दा नांग शहर तक के क्षेत्र में और प्रांत के पूर्वी हिस्सों में क्वांग न्गाई से डैक लक तक भारी और व्यापक वर्षा हुई।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान और जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र ने चेतावनी दी है कि गरज के साथ बारिश के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने, ओलावृष्टि और तेज हवाओं के झोंके आने की उच्च संभावना है, जिससे छोटी नदियों और नालों में अचानक बाढ़, ढलानों पर भूस्खलन और निचले इलाकों में जलभराव हो सकता है; कृषि उत्पादन प्रभावित हो सकता है, पेड़ गिर सकते हैं, घरों, परिवहन बुनियादी ढांचे और अन्य सुविधाओं को नुकसान पहुंच सकता है।
समुद्र में तेज हवाओं और झोंकों के साथ-साथ ऊंची लहरें जहाजों के संचालन और अन्य गतिविधियों को प्रभावित कर सकती हैं।

title: COP31: जलवायु परिवर्तन से निपटने के लिए ठोस उपायों की अपेक्षाएँ। - Vietnam.vn

full_text:
जलवायु परिवर्तन पर संयुक्त राष्ट्र फ्रेमवर्क कन्वेंशन (सीओपी31) के पक्षकारों का 31वां सम्मेलन 9 नवंबर को तुर्की के अंताल्या में शुरू हुआ, जो कि बढ़ती हुई गंभीर चरम मौसम घटनाओं, वैश्विक ऊर्जा सुरक्षा पर बढ़ते दबाव और वैश्विक तापमान वृद्धि को 1.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक सीमित करने के लक्ष्य को प्राप्त करने में बढ़ती कठिनाई की पृष्ठभूमि के बीच हुआ।
लगभग 200 देशों के प्रतिनिधियों की भागीदारी के साथ, यह सम्मेलन, जो 20 नवंबर तक चलेगा, राजनीतिक प्रतिबद्धताओं से हटकर ठोस कार्यान्वयन उपायों की ओर बढ़ने की उम्मीद है।
COP31 में सबसे बड़ी चुनौती कोयला, तेल और गैस सहित जीवाश्म ईंधनों से दूर जाने के लिए एक रोडमैप को बढ़ावा देना था, जबकि कार्यान्वयन की गति और तरीकों पर देश विभाजित रहे।
भू-राजनीतिक तनाव, संघर्ष और ऊर्जा आपूर्ति में व्यवधान के कारण कई देशों ने तत्काल ऊर्जा सुरक्षा को प्राथमिकता दी है, जिससे जीवाश्म ईंधन पर निर्भरता को धीरे-धीरे कम करने के प्रयासों में बाधाएं बढ़ गई हैं।
संयुक्त राष्ट्र की एक रिपोर्ट से संकेत मिलता है कि दुनिया अब औद्योगिक क्रांति से पहले के स्तरों की तुलना में वैश्विक तापमान वृद्धि को 1.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस की सीमा के भीतर रखने के लक्ष्य की ओर अग्रसर नहीं है।
यद्यपि जलवायु परिवर्तन पर 2015 के पेरिस समझौते को अपनाने से पहले के पूर्वानुमानों की तुलना में वर्तमान जलवायु प्रतिबद्धताओं ने दृष्टिकोण में सुधार किया है, फिर भी यदि प्रतिबद्धताओं को पूरी तरह से लागू किया जाता है तो तापमान में वृद्धि 2.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच सकती है।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
इस वर्ष कई क्षेत्रों में सूखे, भीषण गर्मी की लहरों, जंगल की आग और भयंकर बाढ़ ने लक्ष्यों और कार्रवाई के बीच के अंतर को उजागर करना जारी रखा है, जिससे इसके परिणाम तेजी से स्पष्ट हो रहे हैं।
एक अन्य महत्वपूर्ण पहलू तुर्की द्वारा प्रस्तावित विद्युतीकरण कार्यक्रम है। मेजबान देश का लक्ष्य परिवहन, उद्योग और भवनों में बिजली के उपयोग का विस्तार करके 2035 तक कुल वैश्विक अंतिम ऊर्जा खपत में बिजली की हिस्सेदारी को वर्तमान में लगभग 21% से बढ़ाकर 35% करना है।
हालांकि, विशेषज्ञों का कहना है कि विद्युतीकरण से जलवायु को सही मायने में लाभ तभी मिलेगा जब इसके साथ नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा, भंडारण प्रणालियों और पर्याप्त रूप से सक्षम पावर ग्रिड का विकास भी हो।
अंतर्राष्ट्रीय ऊर्जा एजेंसी (आईईए) के अनुसार, 2030 तक मांग को पूरा करने के लिए बिजली ग्रिड में वार्षिक निवेश को वर्तमान 400 अरब डॉलर के स्तर से लगभग 50% तक बढ़ाने की आवश्यकता है।
जलवायु वित्तपोषण एक बड़ी बाधा बनी हुई है। 2024 में अजरबैजान में आयोजित COP29 सम्मेलन में, विकसित देशों ने 2035 तक विकासशील देशों के लिए प्रतिवर्ष कम से कम 300 अरब डॉलर जुटाने की प्रतिबद्धता जताई थी।
हालांकि, वित्तपोषण स्रोतों की पहचान और आवंटन को लेकर अभी भी काफी मतभेद हैं। अनुकूली वित्त विश्लेषणों के आंकड़ों के अनुसार, इस क्षेत्र के लिए अंतरराष्ट्रीय सार्वजनिक वित्तपोषण 2024 में केवल 28.2 बिलियन डॉलर तक ही पहुंचेगा, जबकि विकासशील देशों को सालाना लगभग 305 बिलियन डॉलर की आवश्यकता है।
ट्रम्प प्रशासन द्वारा सहयोग तंत्र से हटने के निर्णय के बाद अंतरराष्ट्रीय जलवायु सहयोग से अमेरिका की निरंतर अनुपस्थिति की पृष्ठभूमि में COP31 का आयोजन हुआ।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
गौरतलब है कि तुर्की इस शिखर सम्मेलन की मेजबानी और अध्यक्षता कर रहा है, जबकि ऑस्ट्रेलिया आधिकारिक वार्ता आयोजित करने के लिए जिम्मेदार है। विश्व नेताओं का यह शिखर सम्मेलन 11-12 नवंबर को दो दिनों तक चलेगा।
COP31 प्रतिबद्धताओं और उनके कार्यान्वयन के बीच के अंतर को पाटने की हमारी क्षमता की परीक्षा होगी, विशेष रूप से जीवाश्म ईंधन से दूर जाने, कमजोर देशों को वित्तीय सहायता प्रदान करने और स्वच्छ ऊर्जा अवसंरचना विकसित करने के क्षेत्रों में।
सम्मेलन के परिणामों का मूल्यांकन न केवल संयुक्त बयानों के माध्यम से किया जाएगा, बल्कि विशिष्ट योजनाओं, संसाधनों और कार्यान्वयन समय-सीमाओं के माध्यम से भी किया जाएगा।

title: 9 नवंबर के लिए मौसम का पूर्वानुमान: उत्तरी वियतनाम में ठंड बढ़ेगी, जबकि मध्य वियतनाम में शीत मोर्चे के कारण भारी बारिश होगी। - Vietnam.vn

full_text:
9 नवंबर के लिए मौसम का पूर्वानुमान: उत्तरी वियतनाम में ठंड बढ़ेगी, जबकि मध्य वियतनाम में शीत मोर्चे के कारण भारी बारिश होगी।
9 नवंबर को उत्तरी वियतनाम में एक शीत मोर्चा आया, जिससे तापमान में अचानक गिरावट आई और ठंड बढ़ गई। कुछ पहाड़ी इलाकों में तापमान 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे चला गया। वहीं, मध्य प्रांतों में व्यापक रूप से भारी वर्षा हुई, कुछ इलाकों में 500 मिमी से अधिक बारिश हुई, जिससे बाढ़ का खतरा पैदा हो गया। समुद्र में, तेज उत्तर-पूर्वी हवाओं के कारण 6 मीटर तक ऊंची लहरें उठीं।
9 नवंबर की सुबह, उत्तरी वियतनाम के पहाड़ी और मैदानी इलाकों में एक ठंडी हवा का प्रकोप हुआ, जिससे कई स्थानों पर बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आया। पूर्वानुमानों के अनुसार, दिन भर ठंडी हवा का यह प्रभाव पूर्वोत्तर के अन्य क्षेत्रों में भी फैलता रहेगा, फिर उत्तर-पश्चिम, उत्तर और मध्य क्षेत्रों तथा दक्षिण-मध्य क्षेत्र के कुछ इलाकों तक पहुँचेगा।
ठंडी हवा के प्रभाव से उत्तरी वियतनाम और उत्तर मध्य वियतनाम में ठंड का मौसम है, जहां न्यूनतम तापमान आमतौर पर 15-18 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहता है, और कुछ पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में तापमान 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे भी जा सकता है। ज़मीनी इलाकों में हवाएं उत्तर-पूर्व दिशा से 3-4 तीव्रता की गति से चलेंगी, जबकि तटीय क्षेत्रों में 5 तीव्रता की गति से चलेंगी, कुछ स्थानों पर यह गति 6 तक पहुंच सकती है और 7 तक तेज़ झोंके आ सकते हैं।
हनोई में 9 नवंबर की सुबह ठंडी हवाएं चलने लगीं, जिससे गरज के साथ मध्यम से भारी बारिश हुई और कुछ इलाकों में बहुत तेज बारिश हुई। तापमान गिरने से राजधानी का मौसम ठंडा हो गया।
विशेष रूप से, मध्य वियतनाम के उत्तरी और मध्य भागों में भारी बारिश हुई, जिससे कई क्षेत्रों में अत्यधिक वर्षा दर्ज की गई। 9 नवंबर को, उत्तरी डेल्टा के दक्षिणी भाग, थान्ह होआ और उत्तरी न्घे आन में मध्यम से भारी बारिश हुई, जिसमें वर्षा की मात्रा आम तौर पर 50-100 मिमी के बीच रही और कुछ स्थानीय क्षेत्रों में 200 मिमी से अधिक हो गई। दक्षिणी न्घे आन में 50-100 मिमी की भारी बारिश हुई, कुछ क्षेत्रों में 150 मिमी से अधिक वर्षा हुई।
हा तिन्ह और उत्तरी क्वांग त्रि में, 9 नवंबर की रात भर भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश जारी रही, जिसमें वर्षा की मात्रा आम तौर पर 100-250 मिमी के बीच रही और कुछ स्थानों पर 350 मिमी से अधिक हो गई।
विशेष रूप से, 9 नवंबर से 10 नवंबर की रात तक, क्वांग त्रि से दा नांग के दक्षिण और क्वांग न्गाई के पूर्व के क्षेत्र में भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश होने का अनुमान है, जिसमें 150-250 मिमी बारिश होगी और कुछ इलाकों में 500 मिमी से अधिक बारिश हो सकती है। जिया लाई और डैक लक के पूर्व में 70-150 मिमी बारिश होगी, कुछ क्षेत्रों में 200 मिमी से अधिक बारिश हो सकती है।
समुद्र में ठंडी हवा के कारण उत्तर-पूर्वी दिशा से तेज़ हवाएँ चल रही हैं और एक विस्तृत क्षेत्र में समुद्र में अशांत लहरें उठ रही हैं। 9 नवंबर की पूरी दिन और रात के दौरान, टोंकिन की खाड़ी और उत्तरी दक्षिण चीन सागर, जिसमें होआंग सा (पैरासेल) द्वीप समूह क्षेत्र भी शामिल है, में 7 की तीव्रता से तेज़ हवाएँ चलेंगी, कभी-कभी 8 की तीव्रता तक भी पहुँचेंगी, और हवा के झोंके 9-10 की तीव्रता तक पहुँचेंगे। लहरों की ऊँचाई 4-6 मीटर होगी, जबकि टोंकिन की खाड़ी में यह 2-4 मीटर होगी।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
पूर्वी सागर और दक्षिणी क्वांग त्रि से क्वांग न्गाई तक फैले उत्तरी समुद्री क्षेत्र में 6-7 तीव्रता की हवाएं चलेंगी, जिनकी तीव्रता 8-9 तक पहुंच सकती है, और लहरें 3-5 मीटर ऊंची होंगी। पूर्वी सागर (जिया लाई से का माऊ तक) और दक्षिण-पश्चिमी पूर्वी सागर, जिसमें ट्रूंग सा (स्प्रैटली) द्वीप समूह का पश्चिमी भाग शामिल है, के दक्षिणी क्षेत्र में 5-6 तीव्रता की हवाएं चलेंगी, जिनकी तीव्रता 7-8 तक पहुंच सकती है, और लहरें 2-4 मीटर ऊंची होंगी।
इसके अलावा, कई समुद्री क्षेत्रों में लगातार बारिश और आंधी-तूफान जारी हैं। आंधी-तूफान के दौरान बवंडर, 7-8 स्तर की तेज हवाएं और 2 मीटर से अधिक ऊंची लहरों का खतरा बना रहता है, जिससे समुद्री गतिविधियों और जहाजों को खतरा हो सकता है।
देश भर के विभिन्न क्षेत्रों के लिए मौसम का पूर्वानुमान:
हनोई में सुबह के समय बादल छाए रहेंगे और मध्यम से भारी बारिश व गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, जिसके बाद बाद में छिटपुट बौछारें पड़ेंगी। उत्तर-पूर्वी हवाएं 3-4 स्तर की होंगी। मौसम ठंडा हो जाएगा। न्यूनतम तापमान 17-19 डिग्री सेल्सियस और अधिकतम तापमान 18-20 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा।
उत्तर-पश्चिमी क्षेत्र में सुबह के समय बादल छाए रहेंगे और छिटपुट बारिश व गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, जिसके बाद कुछ इलाकों में हल्की बारिश हो सकती है। हवाएं हल्की चलेंगी। गरज के साथ बौछारों के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली, ओले और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना है। मौसम ठंडा हो जाएगा। न्यूनतम तापमान 16-19 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, कुछ इलाकों में यह 13 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे भी जा सकता है। अधिकतम तापमान 19-22 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, कुछ इलाकों में यह 22 डिग्री सेल्सियस से ऊपर भी जा सकता है।
उत्तरपूर्वी प्रांतों में सुबह के समय बादल छाए रहेंगे, हल्की बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, मैदानी इलाकों में मध्यम से भारी बारिश होगी; इसके बाद कुछ क्षेत्रों में हल्की बारिश हो सकती है। उत्तरपूर्वी हवाएं 3-4 स्तर की होंगी, तटीय क्षेत्रों में 5 स्तर की और कुछ स्थानों पर 6 स्तर की होंगी, जिनमें 7 स्तर तक के झोंके आ सकते हैं। गरज के साथ बौछारों के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली, ओले और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना है। मौसम ठंडा हो जाएगा। न्यूनतम तापमान 15-18 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, कुछ ऊंचे पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में यह 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे भी जा सकता है। अधिकतम तापमान 18-21 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा।
थान्ह होआ से ह्यू तक आसमान में अधिकतर बादल छाए रहेंगे। उत्तर में (थान्ह होआ और उत्तरी न्घे आन प्रांत में) सुबह के समय मध्यम से भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, कुछ इलाकों में बहुत भारी बारिश होगी, जिसके बाद छिटपुट बारिश होगी। दक्षिण में (दक्षिणी न्घे आन प्रांत से ह्यू शहर तक) भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी। उत्तर से उत्तर-पश्चिम की ओर चलने वाली हवाएं 2-3 तीव्रता की होंगी, तटीय क्षेत्रों में 4-5 तीव्रता की होंगी। गरज के साथ बौछारों के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना है। उत्तर में ठंड रहेगी, जबकि दक्षिण में हल्की ठंड रहेगी। न्यूनतम तापमान 18-21 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा। अधिकतम तापमान 21-24 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, दक्षिण के कुछ इलाकों में तापमान 24 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक हो सकता है।
दक्षिण मध्य तटीय क्षेत्र में बादल छाए रहेंगे, उत्तर में भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आएगा, जबकि दक्षिण में छिटपुट बौछारें और गरज के साथ तूफान आएगा, कुछ क्षेत्रों में स्थानीय रूप से भारी बारिश हो सकती है। उत्तर-पूर्वी हवाएं 3-4 स्तर की रहेंगी। गरज के साथ तूफान के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली, ओले और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना है। न्यूनतम तापमान 22-25 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा। अधिकतम तापमान उत्तर में 26-29 डिग्री सेल्सियस और दक्षिण में 29-32 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
मध्य उच्चभूमि में बादल छाए रहेंगे और कुछ क्षेत्रों में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है। उत्तर-पूर्वी हवाएं 2-3 स्तर की होंगी। न्यूनतम तापमान 19-22 डिग्री सेल्सियस और अधिकतम तापमान 28-31 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा।
दक्षिणी वियतनाम में आसमान में बादल छाए रहेंगे और कुछ इलाकों में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है। उत्तर-पूर्वी हवाएं 2-3 स्तर की होंगी। न्यूनतम तापमान 23-26 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा। अधिकतम तापमान 31-34 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, कुछ इलाकों में यह 34 डिग्री सेल्सियस से भी अधिक हो सकता है।
हो ची मिन्ह सिटी में आसमान में बादल छाए रहेंगे और कुछ इलाकों में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है। उत्तर-पूर्वी हवाएं 2-3 स्तर की होंगी। न्यूनतम तापमान 24-26 डिग्री सेल्सियस और अधिकतम तापमान 32-34 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा।

आईएमडी के मुताबिक आज यानी 9 नवंबर को देश के कई हिस्सों में भारी बारिश के साथ आंधी चल सकती है. मौसम विभाग ने 13 राज्यों में बारिश का अलर्ट जारी किया है. इसमें दिल्ली, बिहार, झारखंड, हिमाचल प्रदेश, पंजाब, जम्मू-कश्मीर, उत्तराखंड, सिक्किम, अरुणाचल प्रदेश, पश्चिम बंगाल और ओडिशा शामिल हैं. मौसम विभाग के मुताबिक तमिलनाडु, पुडुचेरी और कराईकल में हल्की से भारी बारिश तक हो सकती है.
दिल्ली का मौसम-
दिल्ली में भी मौसम धीरे-धीरे करवट ले रहा है. लगातार तापमान में गिरावट दर्ज की जा रही है. 9 नवंबर को दिल्ली में आंशिक रूप से बादल छाए रहेंगे. ज्यादातर इलाकों में धुंध छाई रहेगी. इसके साथ ही तेज हवाएं भी चल सकती है. दिल्ली में 9 नवंबर को अधिकतम तापमान 27 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 14 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा.
यूपी का मौसम-
विभाग के मुताबिक उत्तर प्रदेश के ज्यादातर इलाकों में मौसम सामान्य रहेगा. हालांकि तापमान में गिरावट दर्ज की जा सकती है. राजधानी लखनऊ का अधिकतम तापमान 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 22 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा.
बिहार-झारखंड में बारिश का अलर्ट-
बिहार के ग्रामीण इलाकों में ठंड बढ़ने लगी है. बिहार के कई इलाकों में बारिश हो सकती है. कहीं-कहीं बारिश होने की चेतावनी दी गई है. गया, पटना, भोजपुर, गोपालगंज, जहानाबाद, रोहतास, वैशाली, बक्सर, समस्तीपुर, भागलपुर, खगड़िया, मुंगेर में बारिश हो सकती है. पटना में अधिकतम तापमान 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 22 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा.
झारखंड में भी तापमान में गिरावट दर्ज की जाएगी. राज्य के कई इलाकों में हल्की बारिश हो सकती है. रांची में अधिकतम तापमान 27 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 16 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा.
राजस्थान में कैसा है मौसम-
राजस्थान में जयपुर, झुंझुनू, सीकर, सवाई माधोपुर, चुरू, अजमेर, टोंक, बीकानेर, बूंदी, चित्तौड़गढ़, धौलपुर और भरतपुर में हल्की बारिश हो सकती है. जयपुर में अधिकतम तापमान 33 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 18 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा.
उत्तराखंड और जम्मू-कश्मीर का मौसम-
जम्मू-कश्मीर में कहीं-कहीं बारिश हो सकती है. जम्मू-कश्मीर, लद्दाख, गिलगित-बाल्टिस्तान और मुजफ्फराबाद में बारिश का अलर्ट है. जबकि उत्तराखंड में पिथौरागढ़, उत्तरकाशी, चमोली, रुद्रप्रयाग में बारिश की संभावना है.

After a transformative trip to Iran and one of its mosques, Zirrar started believing in God and writing about the soul of travel. Six years later, Zirrar and his elderly father were participating in the sacred five-day Muslim pilgrimage, the Hajj, when temperatures soared over 51°C. Temperature increases from climate change have made Hajj pilgrimages that happen in the summer, and even during the previously safer spring months, more dangerous.
By the age of 40, I had travelled so much that I was exhausted. I needed to be done with this experimentation of places and see the ultimate place, Mecca. There was always a pull to go back to the east. In my tradition, the only travel you were ever supposed to do is the great pilgrimage to Mecca. Abraham built the very first house of God in Mecca. God said to him: “Proclaim to the people the hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every distant pass.” All souls go to that location; it’s a homecoming. Once I said I was going, my dad said: “OK, I’m going as well.”
A week before the hajj started, I flew into Medina and met my father. Medina becomes a warm-up. You learn the rituals and why you’re doing it. It’s regulating your nervous system to a different routine. It’s very peaceful. To protect you from the sun, they made special umbrellas. It has this coating for the sun. When it gets hot around midday, they release cooling vapour. Now you have shade and there’s water hitting you. There’s a deceptive feeling that it’s not hot.
At the beginning of hajj you go to the Grand Mosque in Mecca and do seven rounds around the Kaaba. It’s hundreds of thousands of people dressed in white, walking like a river and humming supplications to God. I remember covering myself with sunscreen thinking: “I’m going to be hot.” You’re in the open space, no roof, no air conditioning. But the weather was surprisingly cool. Maybe this is one of the blessings of God? I remember thinking: “How am I going to carry an umbrella and push my dad on a wheelchair at the same time?” I threw my umbrella away.
The second day everything shifted. The Day of Arafat. The most sacred day. You start from the outskirts of Mecca. Within two hours of the sun coming up, you start feeling the heat. As it got hotter, almost everybody within my group decided to stay indoors for some of the rituals. There’s a huge canopy set up, and they have air conditioning inside. They were sensible. I was stubborn. I didn’t want to spend this blessed day indoors because of the heat.
If your group hasn’t organised transportation, you have to walk between three places, wearing sandals. They’re quite close to each other, but because of traffic and lack of transportation, half an hour away becomes four hours. People don’t turn off the cars and buses because the air conditioning is keeping them cool. If you walk between buses, you get hit with the heat of diesel. Fumes permeate your nostrils, your skin.
When prayer comes between midday and 4pm, it’s peak heat. You can’t rehydrate or get shade. The heat quickly becomes dangerous. Volunteers give away cold water. I would get a bottle of water and down it in about five seconds, feeling like I’m going to pass out. I couldn’t believe how many water bottles were on the ground. The heat is so incredible, no one has the energy to talk. All you hear is stomping and plastic bottles crunching.
There’s a fight for any shade. There are people sleeping in the compartments where you put the luggage in buses. People are trying to find one little angle where the truck or the car will give you shade. That’s the difference between getting heatstroke and not. Elderly people are passing out under a tree or near the entrance of the mosques.
Normally when an elderly person trips on the street, everyone rushes: “Are you OK? Let me help you up.” Here, that instinct had gone. I saw people who collapsed in the arms of people that they love, realising: “Either I’m going to recover from this heatstroke or I won’t.” You see this resignation in the eyes. That’s the first time I’ve seen people give up on life.
In the places I passed, I remember seeing ambulances but no one coming to help. It just didn’t make any sense. What is their job other than to save people? A lot of people save up their entire life for the hajj and assume they’ll be looked after. But it turns out, here we are in the hottest place, and there’s not enough water, shade and doctors.
I didn’t want to lose my father. As an elderly man, to walk even a mile in the heat was dangerous. I realised I’m responsible for my father; I’ve become the father and he’s become the son. Because of the heat, I would leave him back at the hotel. He performed the essential rites himself. For others, I did them for him, as his son.
I remember feeling drowsy: “I just want to sit down for five minutes.” I remember thinking: “No, don’t sit down.” I’ve read about heatstroke. You don’t wake up from this. If I didn’t find shade, if I didn’t find water, I could easily pass out and I don’t think help would arrive. I’m surrounded by millions of people, but I could still die because of the heat. That’s such a bizarre feeling. My own weakness and vulnerability hit me. I remember my survival kicking in: “I need to just keep going, keep going.”
As the evening approaches, it starts to get a little bit cooler. About 4pm, I climbed Mount Arafat, near where the Prophet Muhammad gave his last sermon, to pray and ask God for forgiveness. Some people chose not to climb because it was hot, but I chose to. On the mountain, I look around and people are smiling, talking, praying. Hundreds of thousands of hands raised into the sky. Here, the heat is completely ignored. People have made peace with themselves, God, and death. This is the first time where I felt at peace. I’ve survived the hottest part of the day.
You spend that night sleeping outside in the open, on pebbles and dirt with thousands of people. We went from being very individualistic people into one cohesive body. At the start of the hajj, I’d seen people jumping queues to get on to buses and fighting. By the end of the five days, you realise: “No one else is going to help us. We have to help each other.” This is no longer: “I’m from country X, therefore I’m more eligible for this than you are.” You give advice, you give your umbrella, you give water. I realised this is what I came for.
Hajj is meant to expose certain pains in your life and you may feel vulnerable. You come back with relief. I watched some of the reporting about people losing their family. I remember feeling quite sad because I didn’t want the hajj to be a hardship in that sense. Historically, there have been many tragedies in hajj: overcrowding, cranes falling, rainstorms. But I’d never heard of so many casualties. These poor people are dying. Where I was, there wasn’t enough water, shade or medical help. Many of these deaths felt avoidable.
I don’t think climate change is something that most people pray about. But, opening your eyes to it, that’s important. In Islam, the world around us is full of God’s signs. Beautiful things point back to him. But we are losing his blessings. Even people who believe in climate change, you can sense there’s a nihilism: “I’m trying, but nothing’s really going to change. What’s really the point of this?” There’s very much a hands-off approach with everything. You say: “This is what God wanted.” But trusting God doesn’t mean doing nothing. The prophet said: “Tie your camel, then trust in God.”

NEW DELHI, Nov 9: A new study has identified an emerging natural process underlying the most extreme heatwaves in mid-latitudes, including northwestern India, in which soil moisture, atmospheric pressure and temperature interact to drive higher temperatures.
Researchers explained that high-pressure systems allow more solar radiation to reach the Earth's surface, heating up the land.
A high-pressure system is a surface area where the atmospheric pressure is higher than the surrounding area.
Likewise, they said, as temperatures rise, soils gradually dry out, reducing their ability to cool the surface through evaporation, which causes the land to heat.
"The two-way relationship between rising temperatures and drying soils has been understood for a while and is already factored into what we expect from a typical extreme heat event," lead author Yinglin Tian, scientist at Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK), said.
"But when we look at these mega heatwaves that have been significantly outstripping previous temperature records, what we're seeing is that once you reach a certain temperature, all three factors: drying soils, high pressure and extreme heat, begin to interact and drive each other further in a way that we haven't understood before," Tian said.
The analysis, published in the journal Science Advances, shows that as the world has warmed from climate change, it has become more likely that the temperature threshold at which this dynamic is triggered is exceeded, forming a vicious cycle, wherein rising temperatures spark off natural processes that cause mercury to climb even further.
Local temperature records have been shattered in heatwave hotspots where "mega heatwaves" have been increasing in frequency faster than more moderate extreme heat events in recent years.
The heatwave hotspots are concentrated in central and eastern Europe, southern Russia and Mongolia, eastern and northwestern North America, northwestern India, the western coast of South America, central and southern Africa, and northern interior Australia.
"We show that a three-way interaction among these components becomes active once a critical temperature threshold is exceeded, contributing, on average, (nearly) 10 per cent to peak temperature anomalies during the most extreme heat events across (nearly) 28 per cent of humid mid-latitude regions," the authors wrote.
The interaction could be systematically underestimated in global climate models, including Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6, they said.
Soils in the climate models are too dry when heat waves are triggered, thereby suppressing subsequent soil-moisture depletion and inhibiting feedback activation, the team said.
They added the findings help explain regional biases in the models related to upper-tail warming, whereby temperatures on the hottest days of a year increase at a significantly faster rate than average or typical temperatures.
"If we're right and this interaction is making the most extreme heat events even hotter, it means we could be in store for more severe future heatwave risks than what is currently expected," co-author Kai Kornhuber, from the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis in Austria, said. (PTI)

In Rajasthan's cities, daytime temperatures were higher than normal on Sunday. In Barmer, the day's maximum temperature crossed 38°C; this is only the second time in the last 10 years that the temperature here has crossed 38°C. In several cities including Jaipur, Chittorgarh, Jaisalmer, Churu, and Ganganagar, the maximum temperature was recorded 2 to 5°C above normal. The Meteorological Department has forecast that the weather will remain clear across the state over the next week, with hot days and cold nights continuing in a similar pattern.
Looking at the weather over the past 24 hours, the sky remained clear with sunshine throughout the day across all cities in the state. On Sunday afternoon, maximum temperatures above 35°C were recorded in Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Barmer, Chittorgarh, Churu, and Bhilwara. The highest maximum temperature on Sunday afternoon was recorded in Barmer at 38.2°C, which was 5°C above normal. The maximum temperature was recorded at 37.5°C in Jaisalmer, 36.2°C in Churu, 35.8°C in Jodhpur, 35.4°C in Chittorgarh, 35.2°C in Bhilwara, and 34.9°C in Pilani.
Why the intense heat during the day?
An anti-cyclonic system has formed over the south-western part of Rajasthan. Under the influence of this system, northern winds are weakening during the day while western winds are strengthening. As a result, the sky remains clear throughout the day alongside bright sunshine, leading to a stronger impact of heat.
Night temperatures rising too, up to 6 °C above normal
Due to the weakening of northern winds caused by the anti-cyclone in the state, nighttime cool conditions are also below normal in several cities. Night temperatures in Barmer, Pali, Jaisalmer, Bikaner, Ganganagar, and Churu remain 3°C to 5°C above normal. On Sunday, Mount Abu recorded the coldest night, where the minimum temperature was recorded at 12.1°C; this is 4°C higher than normal for the location.
Apart from this, the minimum temperature recorded in Fatehpur was 12.4°C and in Sirohi 14.2°C. Meanwhile, in the remaining cities, the minimum temperature stayed above 15°C. In Jaisalmer and Phalodi, the minimum night temperature remained above 22°C.
Temperature rose by up to 1°C in Jaipur
In Jaipur, a rise of up to 1°C was recorded in both day and night temperatures on Sunday. Here too, the sky remained clear throughout the day with bright sunshine. It was warm during the day, whereas there was mild chill in the evening. In Jaipur, the day's maximum temperature was recorded at 33.7°C and the minimum temperature at 19.6°C.
What lies ahead?
The Meteorological Centre, Jaipur has predicted that the sky is likely to remain clear across the state for the next week. Bright sunshine is expected throughout the day during this period, with a possibility of a slight increase in maximum temperatures in some cities.

The insurance industry has long been shaped by its ability to identify, understand, and adapt to new forms of risk. Yet many emerging exposures don’t begin as obvious insurance concerns. Instead, they often arise quietly from technological innovation, shifting consumer behavior, evolving legal frameworks, or changes in the built environment.
Several developments gaining attention today illustrate this dynamic. Increased reliance on geolocation data, the effects of extreme heat on buildings, and the rapid adoption of highly energy-efficient building designs each represent areas where evolving conditions could reshape exposures across multiple lines of business.
Geolocation and Liability
Geolocation data has become a routine feature of modern commerce, powering everything from mobile applications and connected vehicles to targeted advertisements. But as courts and regulators continue to examine the sensitivity of location information, businesses that collect, store, share, or monetize this data may face new questions about privacy obligations and potential liability.
This personal data generally refers to information that identifies or indicates the geographic location of a device, user, or object through technologies such as GPS, IP address tracking, Wi-Fi triangulation, and cellular network signals. Though this has historically been relegated to cellphone usage, geolocation data can now be collected from a wide range of Wi-Fi technologies and Bluetooth-enabled products, from wearable devices and ride-share platforms to robotic lawnmowers.
As a result, a broad range of industries today collect, process, retain, and, in some cases, monetize geolocation information. Retailers and advertising firms, for instance, can now leverage location information to measure foot traffic, analyze consumer behavior, and deliver targeted marketing. Other industries, such as wearable device manufacturers, may use location data to help measure health and physical activity diagnostics, while financial institutions could utilize this data to help detect fraud.
Though no single comprehensive federal privacy law governing the collection and retention of personal data presently exists, a 2026 U.S. Supreme Court ruling could lead to increased judicial sensitivity to the collection and use–or potential abuse–of such data. In Chatrie v. United States, the Supreme Court held that law enforcement’s use of a geofence warrant to obtain a suspect’s personal location data constituted a search under the Fourth Amendment. The decision held that individuals have a reasonable expectation of privacy in their cellphone location records.
As privacy laws, regulatory requirements, and litigation involving geolocation data continue to develop, organizations that collect or use such information may face increased legal, compliance, and risk management considerations, raising the potential for claims, such as cyber, technology errors and omissions, directors and officers, and professional liability exposures.
Heat Risks to Buildings
The record-setting temperatures across much of the U.S. and Europe this summer are just the latest warning sign of a rapidly heating planet. While the human health risks of extreme heat exposure are well documented, high temperatures also have the potential to create specific exposures for multiple lines of business.
According to one study published in the Journal of Engineering (August 2025), curing temperatures can alter concrete’s microstructure, making concrete durability highly sensitive to temperatures that are too hot or too cold. High temperatures can accelerate or inhibit cement hydration, which can then affect several factors that contribute to concrete stability, including pore structure, microcrack development, and permeability.
Steel may face its own heat-related pressures.
A 2025 study published in Buildings, an international, peer-reviewed, open access journal on building science by MDPI, examined how structural steel performed under temperature-humidity cycles and found that humid environments caused corrosion that increased with repeated exposure. The researchers reported that this repeated corrosion damage also substantially reduced the strength, ductility, and fatigue life of steel over time.
If heat is hard on the materials required for building, it’s harder still on the individuals working with them. Construction workers accounted for approximately a third of occupational heat-related deaths between 1992 and 2016–even though they account for around 6% of the overall workforce, according to a 2019 study. Such risks to worker safety may only increase alongside temperatures as heat waves become longer and more frequent across many regions of the U.S.
Less favorable working conditions associated with extreme heat may understandably affect productivity in the construction sector, potentially contributing to insurance implications such as project delays, cost overruns, and heightened safety risks on job sites.
Passive Home, Active Risks?
Rising energy costs and growing interest in lower-carbon living solutions have led many homeowners in recent years to embrace various energy-efficient construction approaches, such as passive housing design. But these designs may have built-in risk for insurers.
A passive house is designed to tightly contain heat during colder months and keep it out during warmer months, while continuously cycling fresh air through the home. The design typically combines a super-insulated envelope with airtight construction methods, incorporates air barriers, and eliminates thermal bridges at junctions while heat recovery ventilation systems supply continuous fresh air.
Proponents suggest that passive building may use up to 90% less heating and cooling energy than conventional construction–a potentially significant incentive for builders and homeowners, considering buildings account for nearly 37% of U.S. energy consumption. That draw is translating into real-world adoption: Phius, a leading certifier of passive houses in the U.S., reported a record 155 design certifications were completed in 2025, with the median project jumping from roughly 6,000-7,000 square feet between 2019 and 2024 to 25,000 square feet–driven in part by a surge in multifamily building projects in states such as New York and Massachusetts.
Yet many of the same features that may contribute to the energy efficiency of passive buildings–such as air tightness and heavy insulation–may also introduce distinct risk considerations. One area frequently discussed is moisture. Due to airtight design, humidity that may have escaped a conventional structure typically must instead be removed mechanically. The American Society of Civil Engineers has identified mold as a potential unintended consequence of certain energy-efficient construction approaches, citing instances where insulation blocked airflow entirely. And while passive design standards generally incorporate hygiene and moisture-control criteria intended to prevent mold, rot, and corrosion, sustained long-term performance may also depend on the proper operation of ventilation and related systems by building inhabitants and property managers.
Overheating has also been identified as a potential concern.
A 2024 review of existing research on passive housing performance found that overheating risks have been reported across numerous climate regions, largely influenced by building characteristics, climate conditions, and occupant behavior. The authors further noted that increasing temperatures and other climate-related factors may only exacerbate those challenges.
While these three risks span different domains, each illustrates how shifting societal, environmental, and technological trends can create new exposures. For insurers, it’s critical to recognize these signals early and adapt strategies to manage potential risks.

Central Queensland has been battered by an intense storm that will likely leave some without power until tomorrow.
Parts of Queensland's Far North are sweltering through an extreme heatwave.
Severe storms have eased in the state's south-east, but are predicted to return from Wednesday.
Emergency crews are assessing damage in central Queensland after a violent thunderstorm unleashed 66,000 lightning strikes around Sarina overnight, snapping power poles and leaving more than 2,000 properties without power.
Ergon Energy described the damage as intense, saying the lightning strikes were within a 100-kilometre radius of the community.
The network said multiple power poles needed replacement and helicopter surveys today would reveal the full extent of the damage.
The Bruce Highway south of Sarina has re-opened after being closed overnight due to fallen wires.
"We're hoping to get power back to some customers by this afternoon, but it's likely to be tomorrow for those in the worst-affected areas," an Ergon spokesperson said.
"The main challenge is the 33kV line from Sarina substation supplying the Koumala area — multiple poles have been snapped and we haven't been able to access the full length of the line to fully understand what we're up against."
Like a 'mini tornado'
Ron Gurnett, who lives at Yukan south of Sarina, said damage to the north was significant.
"It looks like a mini tornado has gone through. I've never seen the golf links like this, there are some big trees uprooted," Mr Gurnett said.
"There's two big poles snapped off and the main powerline to Koumala south is on a 60 degree angle," he said.
The State Emergency Service received a handful of calls about fallen trees and property damage but was unable to assist until this morning due to lightning risks and mobile phone network failures.
Sharon Schofield at Sarina Beach service station said heavy rain sent water under the shop doors, and trees had fallen over local roads.
Heatwave continues
Parts of Far North Queensland are enduring a record-breaking heatwave, as the south-east gets a short break from repeated thunderstorm activity.
The Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) said Weipa, on the Cape York Peninsula, had its hottest November day on record on Saturday, with the mercury tipping 39.8 degrees Celsius.
"Maximum temperatures have been really persisting in quite an exceptional heat around parts of the peninsula," meteorologist Kimba Wong said.
"We've now had 33 days in a row above 36 degrees for Weipa … That is insufferable heat.
"Unfortunately, there's no end to the heat inside this week … that warm and unstable air mass isn't shifting anytime soon."
There is an extreme heatwave warning for the peninsula, while a severe heatwave warning is current for several other regions from the Gulf Country to the Whitsundays.
The BOM said parts of western Cape York Peninsula would have another week of maximum temperatures in the high 30s to low 40s, and overnight temperatures in the mid to high 20s.
Storm pause for SEQ
Localised heavy rainfall and storms are possible around Mackay and the Eungella ranges on Monday.
Ms Wong said south-east Queensland would see a brief reprieve from the storms peppering the region in the past week.
"Entering mid-November now, it's in the midst of our storm season, so it wouldn't go a day without a thunderstorm somewhere in Queensland," she said.
"As we head into Tuesday, Wednesday [and] Thursday, the next trough system starts to push in across the state, so generally a little bit more unsettled weather returning to much of Queensland.
"Perhaps a returning risk of some severe storms across south-east Queensland on Wednesday and Thursday."
Maximum temperatures are forecast to be milder in the south-east on Monday before ramping back up as the week progresses.
"The next slightly cooler change comes through later in the week," Ms Wong said.
Meanwhile, several flood warnings remain active for the state.
There are moderate warnings for flooding along the Barcoo, Bulloo and Upper Balonne rivers.

The People’s Dispensary for Sick Animals (PDSA) warns that dogs can overheat during exercise or simply by being trapped somewhere hot. Puppies, older dogs, overweight animals and flat-faced breeds are particularly vulnerable.
Water and shade
Make sure pets always have access to fresh drinking water, shade and good ventilation. Place water bowls in several accessible spots and check them throughout the day.
Birds, rabbits and guinea pigs also need protection from direct sunlight. Check that cages and enclosures remain shaded as the sun moves.
Rethink walkies
Avoid exercising dogs during the hottest part of the day. On extremely hot days, skip strenuous outings and offer quiet activities in a cool space instead.
Check paving before heading out: if you cannot comfortably hold your hand against it for a few seconds, it is too hot for your dog’s paws. Early mornings and evenings can still be hot, so assess conditions before walking.
Never leave pets in cars
A quick stop at the shops can have deadly consequences for a pet left in a vehicle. Parking in the shade or leaving a window slightly open does not prevent dangerous temperatures from developing.
Sheds, garages, caravans and other enclosed spaces can also trap heat. Check that cats have not slipped inside before closing up.
Know the warning signs
Heavy panting, excessive drooling, weakness, confusion, vomiting or collapse can signal heatstroke in dogs. Do not wait for an animal to collapse before acting.
Cats can also suffer heatstroke, particularly when trapped in hot, poorly ventilated spaces.
Act immediately
If a dog appears to be overheating, stop all activity and move it into shade or a cool, well-ventilated area.
Begin cooling it immediately by gently pouring cool tap water over its body, keeping water away from its nose and mouth. Use a fan or air conditioning to help them cool down and offer drinking water without forcing it to drink.
Do not wrap the dog in a wet towel, as this can trap heat. Contact a vet urgently and continue cooling during transport where possible.
For cats, rabbits and other small pets, handle them gently and contact a vet immediately for cooling advice, taking care not to cause additional stress. A pet with suspected heatstroke needs veterinary attention even if it appears to recover.

CEBU City Mayor Nestor Archival is being urged to consider moving elementary school classes to as early as 5:30 a.m. and shifting to modular learning every Friday as the city prepares for the anticipated effects of the 2026-2027 El Niño.
The proposed adjustment allows pupils to attend face-to-face classes from 5:30 a.m. to 10 a.m. from Monday to Thursday, limiting their exposure to rising temperatures while maintaining classroom instruction.
The proposal follows a meeting on Friday, Nov. 6, where public and private school administrators raised concerns over existing heat-related learning guidelines, seeking greater flexibility in adjusting class hours and learning arrangements.
Proposed schedule
City Councilor Dave Tumulak filed the resolution urging Archival to coordinate with the Department of Education (DepEd) and elementary schools in Cebu City to consider the temporary schedule.
The measure covers public and private elementary schools and recommends Modular Distance Learning (MDL) every Friday to prevent prolonged exposure to extreme heat.
Classroom hours
Under the proposed arrangement, kindergarten pupils would attend three hours of face-to-face classes, while Grades 1 and 2 would have four hours and 20 minutes. Grade 3 pupils would spend four hours and 30 minutes in school, and Grades 4 to 6 would complete six hours of instruction.
The resolution calls for supplementary learning arrangements to cover instructional hours outside the classroom schedule, subject to applicable DepEd policies. This Friday modular setup allows pupils to continue their lessons without attending face-to-face classes.
Tumulak’s measure emphasizes coordinating the adjustments with DepEd and concerned educational institutions while considering instructional requirements and school-level conditions.
School recommendations
During the Nov. 6 meeting, school administrators discussed concentrating classroom instruction in the morning when temperatures are lower. Some representatives raised concerns over differences in classroom capacity, school facilities and learners’ access to suitable environments, which could affect implementation.
Archival said the Cebu City Government will consolidate the recommendations from public and private schools and forward them to the DepEd Central Office for consideration. He noted they will await further discussions between DepEd and the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) before finalizing adjustments.
Learning modalities
Meanwhile, Schools Division Superintendent Nimfa Bongo said several schools in the Cebu City Division have shortened their class periods in response to the heat. She reminded school heads to observe DepEd Memorandum 64, series of 2026, which provides a four-level learning modality framework for managing heat-related disruptions.
Under the framework, schools may adjust learning arrangements depending on prevailing heat conditions, with face-to-face classes suspended at higher heat index levels. Bongo said the division office will meet to clarify implementation concerns and discuss adjustments to class schedules and subject arrangements, while school heads prepare position papers detailing their recommendations for submission to DepEd.
Tumulak’s proposed resolution cited DepEd Memorandum 64, issued on Oct. 26, which outlines anticipatory measures and learning continuity strategies for the 2026-2027 super El Niño. It also referenced Executive Order (EO) 130, issued by the Office of the President on Oct. 28, establishing guidelines for suspending and resuming classes, school activities and onsite work based on prevailing hazards and localized risk assessments.
Under Section 4(b) of the EO, local chief executives, as chairpersons of their respective Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Councils, may declare localized suspensions of face-to-face classes based on documented risk assessments and consultation requirements.
The proposed resolution seeks to have the mayor coordinate with DepEd through the Cebu City Schools Division Office and the affected elementary schools to implement the adjusted schedule. It directs the City Council secretary to furnish copies of the resolution to the mayor, DepEd and other concerned offices for appropriate action.
The measure remains a proposal and does not change existing school schedules. / CAV

Scientists Reach Record Temperature of 9.7 Picokelvins in Orbit
Physicists on China's Tiangong space station measured an equivalent temperature of 9.7 picokelvins, about 280 billion times lower than the background temperature of space. The researchers report in the journal Science that it is the lowest equivalent temperature ever measured.
Scientists reach record temperature of 9.7 picokelvins aboard China's Tiangong space station, according to a paper published in the journal Science. That is 0.0000000000097 kelvins, an equivalent temperature about 280 billion times lower than the background temperature of space.
The researchers call it "to our knowledge, the lowest equivalent temperature ever measured."
How cold is cold
Even empty space is not completely cold. Leftover radiation from the birth of the Universe some 13.8 billion years ago keeps the average background temperature around 2.7 kelvins, or -270.45 degrees Celsius (-454.81 Fahrenheit).
Absolute zero, or zero kelvins, is the theoretical lower limit. Unlike the speed of light, it cannot be reached at all. The closer scientists get, the harder it becomes to remove the remaining thermal energy.
Why the experiment went to orbit
The team wanted to make a Bose-Einstein condensate, an exotic state of matter. It forms when certain atoms are cooled to just fractions of a degree above absolute zero. The atoms then act collectively, their individual quantum states merging into one coherent whole.
That lets researchers study quantum behavior on a much larger scale than single atoms allow. Condensates can also support extremely sensitive measurements of the physical world, potentially helping scientists probe fundamental laws of the Universe.
On Earth, gravity makes it increasingly difficult to cool atoms this far. In orbit, the problem is much smaller.
Previous records
NASA created the first Bose-Einstein condensate in orbit aboard the International Space Station in 2018, cooling a cloud of rubidium atoms to 100 nanokelvins. The previous record stood at 38 picokelvins. It was set during a free-fall experiment in Germany's Bremen Drop Tower and described in a 2021 paper.
The method
Physicists Xiaoji Zhou and Xuzong Chen of Peking University and Weibiao Chen of the Chinese Academy of Sciences led the new work. They used the prolonged microgravity on Tiangong to push cooling further.
They started with a cloud of rubidium-87 atoms, an isotope well suited to laser cooling and to making condensates. Lasers cooled the atoms, which were held in an optical trap inside an apparatus called the Cold Atom Physics Rack.
Next came evaporative cooling. The most energetic atoms are allowed to escape, leaving the rest with less energy. It works much like a cup of coffee cooling as its most energetic molecules leave as vapor.

The Met Office has issued a yellow fog warning for much of England, saying conditions are a "perfect recipe" for thick fog and warning that travel may be disrupted.
The alert runs from 6pm on Sunday until 11am on Monday. It covers most of southern England, excluding the south-west, and the whole of the Midlands.
Where fog is expected
The warning also takes in pockets of northern England and Wales. Fog is expected in Liverpool, Sheffield, York, Cardiff and Wrexham.
Dense fog is forecast mainly inside the warning area. Elsewhere the picture is milder, but not clear.
Niamh Murray, a Met Office operational meteorologist, said: "There is still going to be patchy fog elsewhere, just not quite as dense or as impactful." Parts of the West Country, Northern Ireland and the central belt of Scotland could also see some, she said.
Why fog forms at this time of year
Autumn and winter nights are much longer, Murray explained to the Press Association. That gives temperatures more time to drop.
"We get a longer period of cooling and also the temperatures are much lower," she said. The air also sits closer to the temperature at which fog forms.
What it means for travel
The Met Office has warned that journeys may be disrupted until Monday morning. Drivers, rail passengers and others heading out early across the Midlands and southern England are in the affected zone.
The yellow warning is due to expire at 11am on Monday.

Waterford village still awaiting flood relief measures after Storm Chandra devastation
Senator Joe Conway raised the issues facing Passage East in County Waterford in the Seanad recently
A village in County Waterford is still awaiting flood relief measures that were promised in the aftermath of Storm Chandra, the Seanad has heard.
Independent Senator Joe Conway raised the issue during a recent discussion on flood risk management.
Senator Conway said: “For as long as people can remember, Passage East, County Waterford, has been the victim of regular flooding.
“Last winter, there was an event called Storm Chandra, which I am sure we all remember. It occasioned a lot of flooding all over the country, but particularly in the south east.
“Passage East was decimated by flooding in the early days of February 2026. Two areas, Brookside and Post Office Square, were devastated when the local tributary overflowed.
“We had the unfortunate spectacle of octogenarians out in the street trying to stem the tide as their properties were destroyed.”
He outlined how Minister of State Kevin ‘Boxer’ Moran visited Passage East in the aftermath of the storm.
“On 8 February, the Minister of State, Deputy Moran, took time out of his weekend to come down to talk to the community.
“He listened to their complaints and anger and walked around the town. He talked to people and did a fine job of getting a hands-on appreciation of the situation.
“He was accompanied by a lot of people who knew a lot about the former flooding in Passage East.”
Senator Conway highlighted the promises made by Minister Moran, which he says are yet to be delivered.
“If I remember correctly, he made two commitments to us that morning. There would be money from the Department to provide individual property protections, IPPs, for vulnerable properties.
“I have spoken to my independent colleague on Waterford council, Councillor Declan Barry, who tells me that to the best of his vision and knowledge, those IPPs have not been put in place yet.”
He urged Minister Moran to deliver on his promises before Passage East is hit by further flooding.
“We are now in the flooding and winter season and while lightning may not strike, Passage East will get hit again as sure as eggs are eggs.
“I would simply like the Minister of State to tell me whether the money has been supplied to Waterford City and County Council to provide IPP protection and if the IPPs are in place.”
In response to Senator Conway, Minister Moran said he was very familiar with the situation in Passage East.
He stated: “As the Senator knows, I am very familiar with the flooding and coastal erosion problems across Waterford having visited the county in February of this year.
“I witnessed at first hand the devastation that this event caused to people, businesses and communities, particularly along the east coast and south east coast of Ireland, including Waterford.
“Following the storm event, I met senior officials from eight local authorities to discuss interim measures that could be introduced to provide protection to those areas that were badly impacted by flooding from the storm. This included senior officials from Waterford City and County Council.”
Minister Moran outlined the funding that has been provided to local authorities to address the flooding issues.
“On 30 April, I was delighted to announce the approval of €6.6 million in once-off funding to those eight local authorities to introduce the interim flood protection measures that they had identified in response to the event.
“This included €141,000 for Waterford City and County Council, of which €69,000 is to cover the initial cost of surveying a total of 103 properties for introducing individual property measures.
“These 60 properties in Passage East, and 43 properties in Tallow, were identified by the council to benefit from this IPP, following Storm Chandra.
“The survey reports for these locations have been received from Waterford City and County Council. The survey reports are under consideration by the OPW.”
He concluded by saying that senior officials from the OPW had met representatives of the Waterford City and County Council earlier this week.
Minister Moran added that the OPW expects to revert back to the local authority shortly.

full_text:
By Noah Ebije, Kaduna
As the harmattan season approaches, bringing with it dry vegetation, dusty winds, falling humidity and heightened environmental risks, stakeholders in Kaduna State have raised the alarm over the growing threat of fire outbreaks, calling for urgent preventive measures to protect life, property and the environment.
The warning came against the backdrop of alarming fire statistics released by the Kaduna State Government, which disclosed that the state recorded 306 fire outbreaks in 2025, resulting in 10 deaths, 48 injuries and the destruction of properties estimated at approximately N6.4 billion.
The figures have renewed concerns among environmental advocates, emergency management authorities and other stakeholders about the need to strengthen fire prevention strategies, particularly as the dry season creates favourable conditions for the rapid spread of fires across residential communities, markets, farmlands, forests and other vulnerable locations.
At the centre of the growing campaign is the Kaduna State Climate Change Accountability Mechanism (KADCCAM), which has urged residents to adopt responsible environmental practices and exercise greater caution in their daily activities to prevent fire disasters during the harmattan period.
Co-director of KADCCAM, Ibrahima Yakubu, warned that the combination of dry vegetation, reduced atmospheric moisture and dusty winds associated with harmattan could turn seemingly minor incidents into devastating fires, if precautions were not taken.
He called on residents, particularly farmers, hunters, traders, households and business owners, to exercise greater responsibility when handling fire, cooking equipment, electrical appliances and other potential sources of ignition.
Yakubu specifically cautioned against indiscriminate bush burning, careless disposal of cigarette butts, open-air refuse burning and the storage of highly flammable materials close to heat sources.
He also urged residents to inspect electrical connections regularly, switch off unused appliances, provide basic firefighting equipment where possible and ensure that access roads and emergency exits remain unobstructed.
Beyond the immediate danger of fire outbreaks, KADCCAM expressed concern over environmentally harmful practices that could aggravate the impact of the dry season.
These include indiscriminate waste disposal, open-air waste burning, deforestation, destruction of vegetation and other activities that contribute to environmental pollution and ecological degradation.
The organisation particularly called on farmers and herders to embrace environmentally responsible land management practices, warning against uncontrolled bush burning and the destruction of trees and vegetation.
It stressed that trees and other vegetation play essential roles in maintaining ecological balance, protecting the soil and reducing land degradation, making their preservation particularly important in the face of increasing climate-related challenges.
The environmental warning is reinforced by the disturbing statistics presented by the Deputy Governor of Kaduna State, Dr. Hadiza Sabuwa Balarabe, who called for stronger collaboration among government institutions, businesses, community leaders and residents to improve fire prevention and emergency response.
Balarabe made the call during the opening ceremony of the 2026 National Fire Week, organised by the Federal Fire Service, Kaduna State Command, at the Federal Secretariat Conference Hall, Kawo, Kaduna.
Represented by her Senior Special Assistant on Stakeholder Relations, Engr. Martins Galadima, the Deputy Governor disclosed that Kaduna recorded 306 fire incidents in 2025, claiming 10 lives and leaving 48 persons injured, while destroying properties valued at approximately N6.4 billion.
Although she acknowledged that the number of incidents had declined considerably from the 523 recorded in 2019, she expressed concern that fire outbreaks had continued to average about 300 annually over the past three years.
For the Deputy Governor, the figures represent more than statistics; they reflect the human and economic consequences of preventable disasters and the urgent need for a more safety-conscious society.
She stressed that fire prevention must not be regarded as the exclusive responsibility of firefighters and emergency management agencies but as a collective obligation requiring the active participation of every citizen.
“Fire prevention should be regarded as a collective responsibility rather than a duty left exclusively to firefighters and emergency response agencies,” she emphasised.
According to her, electrical faults, improper use of electrical appliances, careless handling of fire, unsafe storage of flammable materials and indiscriminate bush burning remain some of the major causes of fire outbreaks.
She maintained that most of these incidents could be prevented through responsible behaviour, compliance with safety regulations and the adoption of simple but effective fire prevention measures.
As part of measures to minimise the danger, Balarabe urged households to conduct regular inspections of their electrical installations, avoid overloading sockets and switch off electrical appliances before going to bed.
She also advised residents to exercise extreme caution when handling cooking gas, kerosene and other combustible materials.
For business owners, market associations and petroleum station operators, the Deputy Governor emphasised the need to maintain functional fire extinguishers, provide accessible emergency exits and organise regular fire safety training for employees.
She further urged business operators to comply strictly with established fire safety regulations, noting that negligence and failure to observe basic safety standards could expose workers, customers and surrounding communities to unnecessary danger.
The call is particularly significant for markets and densely populated commercial areas, where combustible materials, electrical installations and human activities often combine to create potentially dangerous conditions.
She noted that a fire outbreak in such locations can spread rapidly, destroying shops, businesses and livelihoods within minutes, while placing lives at serious risk.
While prevention remains the first line of defence, the Kaduna State Government has also emphasised the importance of strengthening institutional capacity to respond effectively whenever emergencies occur.
Balarabe called for improved coordination among the Federal Fire Service, Kaduna State Fire and Public Safety Service, Kaduna State Emergency Management Agency (KADSEMA), National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other relevant emergency response institutions.
She observed that a coordinated emergency response system, supported by adequate equipment, professional training and timely communication, would significantly improve the state’s ability to manage fire disasters.
The Deputy Governor commended officers and men of the Federal Fire Service for their courage, professionalism and dedication to protecting lives and property.
She also called on government institutions, corporate organisations and members of the public to support emergency response agencies through cooperation, adequate resources and responsible conduct.
The 2026 National Fire Week, she noted, provided an important platform for promoting public awareness, strengthening institutional partnerships and encouraging citizens to embrace fire safety practices in their homes, workplaces, markets and communities.
One of the highlights of the event was a series of practical fire simulation exercises demonstrating the operational preparedness, technical competence and combat readiness of Federal Fire Service personnel in handling fire emergencies.
While fire outbreaks remain a major concern during the Harmattan season, environmental advocates warn that the period also presents other challenges that require adequate public attention.
The dry and dusty conditions associated with Harmattan can increase exposure to airborne dust and worsen discomfort for people with respiratory sensitivities.
KADCCAM has therefore encouraged residents to reduce unnecessary exposure to dust, maintain proper hygiene, keep water sources clean and take appropriate precautions to protect vulnerable groups, particularly children, older persons and people with respiratory sensitivities.
The organisation also warned that indiscriminate waste burning and vegetation destruction could compound environmental challenges by worsening air pollution and undermining the natural protection provided by trees and other vegetation.
For farmers, hunters and herders, the warning is particularly relevant, as uncontrolled burning of bushes and farmlands during the dry season could quickly spread beyond intended areas, threatening settlements, farms, livestock, forests and other valuable environmental resources.
KADCCAM’s position is that environmental protection must be integrated into everyday activities rather than treated as an occasional campaign.
The emerging consensus among stakeholders is that preventing fire outbreaks and reducing environmental hazards require more than government directives or the periodic activities of emergency response agencies.
It demands a change in public attitude, greater environmental awareness and sustained collaboration among institutions and communities.
KADCCAM emphasised that preventing environmental disasters is a shared responsibility involving government institutions, traditional and religious leaders, community associations, civil society organisations and individual residents.
It urged residents to promptly report fire outbreaks and other environmental emergencies to the appropriate authorities rather than attempting to tackle dangerous situations without adequate training or firefighting equipment.
The warning is especially important during Harmattan, when dry vegetation and windy conditions can cause small fires to spread rapidly, leaving little time for intervention.
Ultimately, the challenge before Kaduna State is not simply how to respond when fires break out but how to prevent them from occurring in the first place.
With 306 recorded fire incidents, 10 deaths, 48 injuries and property losses estimated at N6.4 billion in 2025, the consequences of inadequate fire safety awareness are already evident.
Stakeholders agreed that as the state enters another Harmattan season, residents, farmers, hunters, traders, business operators and public institutions must recognise that seemingly minor acts of negligence can have devastating consequences.
As the Deputy Governor rightly emphasised, the most effective way to fight fire is to prevent it.
For KADCCAM, the message is equally clear: environmental responsibility must become a daily commitment.
Protecting trees, avoiding indiscriminate bush burning, reducing pollution, observing fire safety precautions and keeping communities clean are not merely environmental obligations; they are essential investments in public safety, sustainable livelihoods and a more climate-resilient Kaduna State.
